input.question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure if you're going to get a proper ELI5 answer to this: understanding why things run that fast requires understanding how computers are designed and the network architecture of the Internet - not exactly light reading. But to give more details about investors: yes, investment firms will pay out the nose for real estate as close to the stock exchange as possible, so that their trading servers will have as little lag as they can. Every last millisecond counts.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a big game together in a playground. You all want to know where everyone is and what they are doing, right? If everyone just shouts out what they are doing, it would be super confusing and noisy!

Now, imagine there is a super smart teacher (that’s the computer server) in the middle of the playground. Every time you do something—like run, jump, or pick up a toy—you tell the teacher what you did. The teacher listens to everyone and quickly tells everyone else what is happening. So, you all see each other running and jumping at the same time, without getting mixed up.

Online games like CoD or WoW have lots and lots of players. But they use super-fast computers and special rules (called “protocols”) to make sure everyone’s actions are shared quickly and correctly, just like the teacher in the playground. That’s how everyone’s game looks the same and works together so fast!
